site_process.notes: Pilot/demonstration scale: 'set to process 75 tons per annum (tpa) of black mass' (2023). Status: Q2 2026 release (B4) 'continued operating the Innovation Center and demonstration plant'.
Phase 1 '3,000 MT of black mass per year at full capacity' (B6); B7 says '3,000 metric tons of spent LiB input material'. Property sale closed 2025-06-12 (B2); never built.

'one unit installed can process up to 3,100 tonnes of scrap materials to produce up to 900 tonnes of MHP per year' (input = black mass and other nickel scrap). Start resolved: operations began 2024-04-10 (B13, same date as 48C release B14); ribbon cutting Sept 2024 (B15). Status: 'began operations in 2024 ... completed 3,400 production hours' (B12, 2026-08-20).
'refine up to 24,000 metric tons of domestic black mass annually' into MHP and Li2CO3; 'operational as early as 2029' (B12; March release said 2028). Site still under assessment (B19, 2026-09-22).

Black mass leaching to pCAM/Li2CO3/graphite. Input capacity not stated in any opened source (earlier '2 t black mass/day' came from an unopened energy-storage.news snippet; Manufacturing Dive B22 states 2 t/day as pCAM output - see precursor row). Status: Sept 2025 LOI refers to NCM hydroxide 'produced ... at Green Li-ion's U.S. facility in Atoka' and a mass production trial; no 2026 source found.

Unit = metric tonnes of pCAM per DAY: 'expected to produce two metric tons of pCAM per day, with plans to quadruple capacity within the year' (April 2024). Conflict resolved in favour of pCAM output (opened source). Expansion unconfirmed; EcoPro LOI (B24) says supply would 'underpin a significant expansion'.

'initially process approximately 10,000 tons of scrap lithium-ion batteries per annum' (Casa Grande alone, 2023 Q&A). Feb 2023 release (B29) phrased it as 10,000 t of recycled material; April 2025 Ecobat release (B30) gives 'up to 10,000 tons' for all three plants combined - scope conflict remains. Start resolved: 'Commissioned April 2024' (B30, Ecobat); pv magazine's April 2025 'comes online' (B31) reports that announcement. pv magazine: 2,000-4,000 t recycled material expected in 2025; wet shredding under inert gas to black mass.
